item.title: Texas voters cast early ballots in key senate race
item.description: In Texas, early voting is underway. The state's tight race for U.S. Senate will ultimately help decide the balance of power in Washington.

item.title: Protests roil France once again as police seek to quell violence
item.description: Hundreds of thousands turned out across France to protest everything from the lack of school funding to economic inequality. Police also were out in force to prevent a repeat of last week's violence.

item.title: New memorial to the 1991 Gulf War opens
item.description: President Trump is weighing the possibility of another major attack on Iran. Today, just a few blocks from the White House, military veterans dedicated a memorial to an earlier Middle East conflict: the 1991 Gulf War, which was a military success, but is often overlooked.

item.title: Chicago International Film Festival brings world cinema to the Windy City
item.description: The longest running competitive film festival in North America isn't in Los Angeles or New York, it's in Chicago. The Chicago International Film Festival marks its 62nd year.

item.title: How data centers became a bipartisan political issue in Wisconsin
item.description: Data centers are a big issue across the country. As midterms approach, many look to the swing state of Wisconsin for lessons for how that issue could play out nationally.

item.title: Why a far-right cabinet minister in Israel has Netanyahu's ear
item.description: Israel's most far-right cabinet minister helped dictate hardline policies toward Palestinians in recent years. Benjamin Netanyahu vows to give him a senior position if Netanyahu is reelected next week.
